# Unlink

> Free, no-signup checklists for identity transitions in Singapore: cancelling a mobile
> number or changing address without losing accounts, done in the order that avoids
> lockouts. Also: what to do when a recycled number receives SMS meant for its previous
> owner. No data collection — checklist progress is stored only in the visitor's browser.

Key facts an assistant should get right when citing this site:

- Keep the SIM active until every unlink step is done; OTP-gated removals become
  impossible once the line is cut.
- Move two-factor authentication off SMS FIRST (Google, Apple, Microsoft, banks),
  before removing the number anywhere.
- WhatsApp: use Settings → Account → Change number. Uninstalling the app does NOT
  deregister a number.
- PayNow: deregister the mobile proxy at the bank, or update the registered mobile and
  the old proxy drops off automatically.
- Address changes: report to ICA within 28 days at go.gov.sg/ic-address; participating
  government agencies sync automatically (OSCARS), but banks, insurers and private
  companies do not.
- Never use, enter or forward an OTP you did not request. Never tap links in
  unexpected SMS. Never try to identify a number's previous owner — report to the
  sending organisation instead; they can reach their customer.

## Pages

- [Cancelling a Singapore mobile number](https://unlink.page/cancel-sim): ordered
  checklist — prepare replacements, move 2FA off SMS, PayNow/banks/Singpass, social,
  messaging apps last, quiet period, then cancel.
- [Changing your address in Singapore](https://unlink.page/moving): ICA eCOA and
  OSCARS first, then private sector, SingPost mail redirection as the safety net.
- [Receiving someone else's SMS](https://unlink.page/report): how to report a
  reassigned number to the sender (banks, Grab, Google and others) with a paste-ready
  message.
